title: Modular SKU Architecture and Launch Brief
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This brief defines a modular SKU architecture for Redwood’s inference surface that (1) decouples fidelity, latency tier, and capacity primitives into composable SKUs, (2) simplifies enterprise procurement and migration from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private, and (3) enables per-route SLO crediting and clear upgrade ladders. The proposal targets the Optimize, Hosted API, and Dedicated product lines and is intended for product, pricing, sales, and revenue ops review.

Background and motivation

- Current challenges: monolithic bundles that mix latency guarantees, capacity reservations, and fidelity add-ons make upgrades and cost forecasting difficult for customers and the sales motion.
- Objectives: make consumption predictable, enable programmatic upgrades, un-block enterprise procurement, and reduce friction for self-serve developers.

Key principles

1) Composability: customers should be able to purchase primitives and combine them into the service profile they need.
2) Predictable economics: SKU math maps directly to token-minute and session-credit estimators.
3) SLO alignment: each SKU exposes the SLOs it represents and is credit-anchored.
4) Migration-first: provide upgrade paths and credit conversion rules from existing bundles.

Proposed SKU taxonomy (primitive-level)

- Base compute SKU: compute.{latency-tier}.{vCPU/GPU-class}
  - latency-tier: fast | standard | low-cost
  - GPU-class: g4x | a10 | h100
  - Example: compute.fast.h100

- Fidelity SKU: fidelity.{quality-tier}
  - quality-tier: premium | balanced | quantized
  - Use: toggled per-route; attaches cost multiplier to compute SKU

- Capacity SKU: capacity.{reserved|burst}.{hours}
  - reserved: monthly commitment (for Dedicated)
  - burst: on-demand credit bucket linked to reserved SKU

- Session SKU: session.{minute|per-call}
  - session.minute: charged per active session-minute for stateful chat workloads

- Telemetry & Observability SKU: telemetry.{retention}.{sampling}
  - retention: 7d | 30d | 90d
  - sampling: full | 10pct | 1pct

SKU matrix (cost mapping examples)

| SKU | Unit | Example price band (USD) | SLOs represented |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| compute.fast.h100 | token-second | $0.00012/token-sec | p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms |
| fidelity.premium | multiplier | x1.8 | semantic quality regression < 0.5% |
| capacity.reserved.720h | month | $45k / month | 99.95% uptime, priority bursting |
| session.minute | minute | $0.02 / min | session stickiness, KV retention 12h |
| telemetry.30d.full | GB / mo | $0.015 / GB | 30d retention, trace search SLA 24h |

Note: price bands above are illustrative and will be validated by finance for commercial launch.

Packaging patterns (pre-built bundles for common buyer personas)

- Developer Sandbox (self-serve): compute.standard.a10 + fidelity.balanced (pay-as-you-go) + telemetry.7d.10pct
- Production API (SaaS product teams): compute.fast.a10 + capacity.reserved.240h + fidelity.balanced + telemetry.30d.10pct
- Enterprise SLA (regulated): compute.fast.h100 + capacity.reserved.720h + fidelity.premium + telemetry.90d.full + private-control-plane add-on

Billing model and metering rules

- Metering primitives: compute token-seconds (primary), session-minutes (stateful), telemetry GB, capacity-hour commitments.
- Rounding & minimums: per-1-second compute rounding for token-seconds; session-minutes rounded to nearest 6s; monthly reserved capacity billed pro-rata on subscription start.
- Credits and conversions: provide a conversion matrix to migrate customers from legacy bundles to modular SKUs (example: legacy-commit-100k -> converts to capacity.reserved.240h + $X in migration credits).

Upgrade and migration playbook (sales + self-serve)

1) Discovery: map current consumption to primitives using the consumption-mapper script (example CLI below).
2) Recommend: proposer service returns suggested primitives and delta cost with fidelity risk estimate.
3) Trial: enable 14-day trial of fidelity.premium and capacity.burst paired with automated rollback to balanced fidelity.
4) Convert: one-click upgrade in Console with credit-offset rules and contract amendment workflow for Reserved SKUs.

CLI example: consumption mapper (illustrative)

```
$ redwood consumption-map --tenant T123 --period 30d --output csv
# Output columns: route, avg_tokens_per_call, peak_rps, session_minutes
```

SLO and product contracts (how SKUs map to commitments)

- Each compute SKU publishes target latency p50/p95 and a cost-of-failure SLA credit percentage. Example SLA: compute.fast.* has p95 target and 0.1% monthly availability credit if missed.
- Fidelity SKUs include a quality gate: experiments in the shadow-eval harness must show no more than X% regression on customer prompt sets.

Launch sequence and milestones (quarterly phased rollout)

- Q2 2026 (Pilot): internal alpha with three enterprise customers; validate conversion rules and Console UX.
- Q3 2026 (Beta): self-serve small-to-medium customers; public docs and pricing estimator; enable auto-suggestions in Console.
- Q4 2026 (GA): full rollout, marketing enablement, sales training, and partner enablement.

Metrics and success criteria

- Commercial metrics: % of new bookings with modular SKUs, migration conversion rate, average revenue per tenant change.
- Operational metrics: metering accuracy > 99.9%, Console upgrade success rate > 98%.
- Quality metrics: fidelity regression incidents (monthly) < 1 for pilot customers.

Risk assessment and mitigations

- Risk: customer confusion with many primitives. Mitigation: pre-built bundles and Console "Suggest" flow, robust UI defaults.
- Risk: billing disputes due to conversion. Mitigation: migration credit escrow and stepwise conversion with invoice preview.
- Risk: fidelity regressions after quantization multipliers. Mitigation: shadow-eval gate and staged canary.

Implementation notes for engineering

- Metering: extend runtime-meter to emit compute.token_seconds and session.active_minutes with tenant tags. Owner: runtime-metrics-team.
- Console: add SKU builder UI, suggestion endpoint, and amortized cost preview. Owner: console-web-team.
- Billing: billing-engine must accept SKU-change events and produce pro-rata invoices; add conversion API. Owner: billing-team.

Open questions (to resolve before GA)

1) Exact fidelity multipliers per model family and quantization profile (research + finance).
2) Default downgrade/rollback policy for fidelity auto-prefetch.
3) How to expose SKU-level credits on customer invoices (UX + legal).

Appendix A: Example migration scenario

- Customer: SaaS analytics vendor with legacy bundle L-Enterprise (250k tokens/day predictable).
- Consumption mapping: maps to compute.standard.a10 + session.minute 3,000 monthly.
- Recommended plan: convert to capacity.reserved.240h + compute.fast.a10 for peak routes + fidelity.balanced for background jobs.
- Credit: offer 10% migration credit for first 3 months and one-time onboarding discount.

Appendix B: Console mock flows (text)

1) Onboarding modal: "Map your current consumption" -> runs consumption-mapper -> shows recommended bundle with cost delta and "Try trial" button.
2) SKU builder: drag-and-drop primitives, see live SLO badges and monthly estimate.
